Estimate a window transition network analysis (WTNA) model

Source: R/build_aliases.R
build_wtna.Rd

build_network(method = "wtna"), or for short build_wtna(), estimates a window transition network analysis (WTNA) model from one-hot codes. The rows are cut into windows of window_size rows, and the edge from code A to code B counts the times B is active in the window after one where A is active.

Windows do not cross actors (actor) or sessions (session). build_network(method = "wtna_cooccurrence") counts the codes active in the same window instead; wtna() returns both networks at once.

Usage

build_wtna(
  data,
  codes = NULL,
  window_size = 3L,
  mode = c("non-overlapping", "overlapping"),
  type = c("frequency", "relative"),
  actor = NULL,
  session = NULL,
  metadata_cols = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  scaling = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  labels = NULL,
  params = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

One-hot data: one row per time point and one column of 0 and 1 per code.

codes

The code columns (one per state, 1 when the state is active). Default NULL: every column outside the other roles.

window_size

How many consecutive rows form one window. Default 3.

mode

"non-overlapping" (default) or "overlapping" windows: overlapping ones slide by one row, as tna::import_onehot(window_type = "sliding"), and are counted in blocks of window_size.

type

"frequency" (default) keeps the counts; "relative" divides each row by its sum.

actor

The column naming who each row belongs to; windows do not cross actors. Default NULL.

session

The column identifying sessions; windows do not cross sessions. Default NULL.

metadata_cols

Columns to keep as the network's metadata, never read as codes. Default NULL.

group

A column to split the data by: one network per value, returned as a netobject_group. Default NULL.

scaling

Rescaling applied to the weights after estimation, in the order given: "minmax" rescales the weights to run from 0 to 1, over every cell for the transition methods (tna's rule, so with no zero cell the smallest weight becomes 0) and over the non-zero weights, into (0, 1], for the other methods, "max" divides by the largest absolute weight, "rank" replaces the non-zero weights by their ranks, and "normalize" makes each row's absolute weights sum to 1; an undirected network whose matrix it makes asymmetric becomes directed, so both of a pair's values are kept as edges. Zero weights stay zero under every option. Combine them as in c("rank", "minmax"). Default NULL (none).

threshold

Weights whose absolute value is below this are set to zero. Default 0 (none).

labels

New display labels for the nodes, applied after estimation: a two-column data frame (name, label), a named character vector c(name = "label") or a named list. It rewrites the node labels and the weight matrix's dimnames; nodes not listed keep their names. Default NULL.

params

Settings for the estimator, as a named list. The network keeps them. Default list().

...

Further arguments for build_network(). method cannot be given (error of class nestimate_bad_input).

Value

A netobject (a netobject_group with group), as build_network() returns it.

See also

build_network() for every method; wtna() for the transition and co-occurrence networks together; action_to_onehot() to turn an event log into one-hot codes.

Examples

codes <- c("Reading", "Video", "Forum", "Quiz", "Coding", "Review")
build_network(learning_activities, method = "wtna", codes = codes,
              actor = "student")
#> Window TNA (transitions) [directed]
#>   Weights: [2493.000, 4314.000]  |  mean: 3025.056
#> 
#>   Strongest edges (10 of 36):
#>    from    to      weight
#>    Video   Video   4314  
#>    Reading Reading 4297  
#>    Review  Review  4206  
#>    Coding  Coding  4005  
#>    Forum   Forum   3881  
#>    Quiz    Quiz    3695  
#>    Review  Video   3113  
#>    Coding  Video   3094  
#>    Video   Review  3018  
#>    Reading Review  3008   
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix.
build_wtna(learning_activities, codes = codes, actor = "student")
#> Window TNA (transitions) [directed]
#>   Weights: [2493.000, 4314.000]  |  mean: 3025.056
#> 
#>   Strongest edges (10 of 36):
#>    from    to      weight
#>    Video   Video   4314  
#>    Reading Reading 4297  
#>    Review  Review  4206  
#>    Coding  Coding  4005  
#>    Forum   Forum   3881  
#>    Quiz    Quiz    3695  
#>    Review  Video   3113  
#>    Coding  Video   3094  
#>    Video   Review  3018  
#>    Reading Review  3008   
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix.
